memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But Joseph said, 'Far be it from me to do such a thing! Only the man who was found to have the cup will become my slave. The rest of you, go back to your father in peace.'" — Gen 44:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is the sharpest edge of Joseph's test. He is offering them the perfect escape. Leave Benjamin. Go home free. No penalty, no blame, no cost.

It is the exact situation from twenty years ago, recreated in every detail. Rachel's son is about to disappear into slavery in Egypt. The other brothers can walk away clean and tell their father whatever story they like. Nobody would ever know.

Joseph needs to see what they will do with the door held wide open.

God's tests often come to us the same way — not as obvious temptations, but as easy exits. A convenient silence. A friendship you could quietly let fade. A responsibility you could reasonably hand to someone else. Nobody would blame you. Nobody would even notice.

Those are the moments that reveal who we have become. Character is not what we do when we are watched; it is what we do when leaving would cost us nothing.

Jesus faced the ultimate open door. He could have called twelve legions of angels and walked away from the cross (Matt 26:53). Every escape was available to Him. He stayed — for us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "easy exit" is in front of you right now?
2. Who has God placed in your life that you are responsible to stand with?
3. How does it move you that Jesus refused every escape route on your behalf?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You could have walked away from the cross and You stayed for me. Give me that same steady love, so that I do not abandon the people You have given me to stand beside. Amen.
